name: Volo (CloudWeGo Rust RPC framework)
baseline: Kitex (Go RPC framework implementing Thrift/gRPC protocols)
workload: QPS benchmark 'under the same test conditions as Kitex', limited to 4 CPU cores (4C), on an RPC echo-style workload using Volo's Thrift/gRPC-compatible transport
claimed_speedup: "Under the same test conditions as Kitex (limited to 4C), the Volo QPS is 350k; at the same time, we are internally verifying the version based on Monoio ..., and the QPS can reach 440k."
tradeoffs: Rust vs. Go (Kitex); Volo implements both Thrift (volo-thrift) and gRPC (volo-grpc) protocols itself rather than replacing a generic incumbent wholesale; a separate Monoio-runtime-based variant is described as still 'internally verifying' (not the shipped default).
caveats: The README explicitly self-hedges the comparison: "it is very unfair to compare the performance with the Go framework, so we will not focus on comparing the performance of Volo and Kitex ... I hope everyone can view it objectively" and "we hope to weaken the comparison of performance data as much as possible, and we'll only publish our own QPS data." No Kitex-side QPS number is given on the same page for direct comparison, and no CPU model or compiler flags are stated -- first-party claim with partial methodology, capped at Tier C. Baseline is Kitex (a widely-used ByteDance incumbent, itself already cataloged on KNOWN_LIST) rather than gRPC/Thrift/uWebSockets directly, so baseline_in_list=false and confidence is reduced accordingly.
found_via: Blogs / talks: HN Algolia query "zero-copy protobuf rust" -> HN item 47801200 ("Zero-copy protobuf and ConnectRPC for Rust") comment thread naming https://github.com/cloudwego/volo as a 4-year-old Rust zero-copy gRPC/Thrift implementation; opened the repo's README Performance section directly

name: cmd-stream (TCP + MUS codec) -- third-party benchmark vs gRPC/Protobuf
workload: Echo requests over TCP: 1/2/4/8/16 concurrent Go clients, each firing all requests simultaneously in separate goroutines, payload sizes 17-1024 bytes, fixed 30ms server-side response delay; QPS benchmark run via `go test -bench BenchmarkQPS`
claimed_speedup: cmd-stream (TCP, MUS codec) 145352 QPS at 1 client vs grpc_http2_protobuf 46142 QPS (~3.15x), and 288727 QPS at 16 clients vs grpc_http2_protobuf 63285 QPS (~4.56x) (derived from page data, results/qps/qps.csv)
compiler_and_flags: Go 1.24.1, default `go test -bench` build (no explicit -gcflags / optimization flags stated beyond the Go toolchain version)
hardware: AMD Ryzen 7 PRO 5850U with Radeon Graphics, Debian 6.1.148-1 x86_64 GNU/Linux (laptop, charger connected, fan at full speed)
tradeoffs: Independent third-party benchmark repo (by ymz-ncnk, likely the mus-format/cmd-stream author) rather than a peer-reviewed or vendor-neutral suite; also exercises cmd-stream's own MUS serialization format (also KNOWN_LIST) rather than isolating transport from codec.
caveats: cmd-stream/cmd-stream-go and mus-format/mus-go are both already on KNOWN_LIST; reported here only as new Tier A evidence of cmd-stream (using MUS) beating the in-scope baseline gRPC, per the orchestrator's is_evidence_for_known exception. Benchmark is single-laptop, single-run-family (10 iterations via -count=10) rather than datacenter-scale; DRPC (a different framework in the same suite) is separately noted to hit a head-of-line-blocking ceiling, but that does not apply to the cmd-stream vs gRPC numbers cited here.
found_via: Blogs / talks: HN Algolia query "faster than gRPC" -> GitHub Show HN link https://github.com/cmd-stream/cmd-stream-go ("3x faster than gRPC") -> opened linked companion repo https://github.com/ymz-ncnk/go-client-server-communication-benchmarks and its results/qps/qps.csv
